body: READ-ONLY DESIGN DISPOSITION on the eligible-set carrier: do not keep bare `supportWeight = 1.0` for a genuinely empty eligible set. Current source already exposes why. `scaleToEligible`/`supportOf` use `eligible.isEmpty` as an undeclared-eligibility sentinel (`cost.scala:751-767`), while external rows also have no eligible content terms; one `Set.empty` therefore denotes two different states. `CostBreakdown` documents 1.0 as 'nothing was assumed' (`:249-258`), but `AlignWire.costBreakdown` says zero is the honest value when nothing eligible was measured and explicitly calls 1.0 fabrication (`wire.scala:302-309`). Adding the set without separating `Undeclared` from `Declared(Set.empty)` preserves this contradiction, and scalar-only consumers can still rank `(1.0,{})` above measured source rows. Narrow robust shape: make eligibility declaration total at construction (remove the empty default/sentinel), carry `eligibleTerms`, validate `terms.keySet subsetOf eligibleTerms`, and represent the derived ratio as `NoEligibleTerms | Fraction(value)` (or `Option[Double]` if an ADT is too wide). External rows then have `NoEligibleTerms`, not maximal support; source rows have a finite fraction. If compatibility requires an undeclared state, model it explicitly rather than overloading empty. Since this already forces hsmm/v4, fixing the denominator state now is cheaper and scientifically clearer than preserving a scalar whose order is invalid. No files edited.
